title: Stage 2 actor service observation architecture
purpose: Add bounded connection-local actor service evidence without installing a work-quantum policy or changing shard scheduling.
design_summary: A connection can independently opt into actor-service and buffer-copy ObserveOnly sinks. The existing shard records a compact immutable actor value after each complete transition and effect dispatch. Existing ownership boundaries record legacy_current retry copies, oversized raw queue copies, formatted payloads, combined payloads, sent-plaintext retention, owned path-migration retransmission clones, and receive-segment insertion or capacity reuse with logical and copied bytes, segment and capacity counts, join scope, versions, reason, latch, lifecycle, and explicit missing state. A configure-once connection-local operation observer links the retransmission queue and stream bookkeeping to the runtime evidence sink; both producer and sink failures are guarded so they cannot affect progress or ownership. Fixed-field v2 accumulators build bounded summaries while retained v1 schemas remain immutable. The legacy shard drain and copy/ownership paths remain the only applied behavior.
data_and_state_considerations: The observations and accumulators use enums, immutable record structs, fixed scalar fields, and connection-local accumulator locks. They introduce no per-packet dependency injection, dictionary, model, global lock, or unbounded state. The application-send queue, sent-packet store, and retransmission queue maintain total retained count, capacity, and oldest time at existing ownership transitions so their total retention snapshots no longer scan; application-send queue-cause and sent-packet storage or packet-number-span detail remain diagnostic scans. Missing runnable-connection count, oldest shard item age, deadline lateness, reviewed useful-work units, exact buffer release, retained age, and pool outstanding state remain explicit. Wake grouping is complete only when the run manifest proves full-shard observation coverage.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Observation may measure existing follow-on counts but cannot limit or defer them.
A throwing or rejecting sink cannot interrupt transition, effect, ownership release, cancellation, disposal, recovery, timer, or terminal work.
Queue delay is not oldest-shard-item age, pending work-item count is not runnable-connection count, and timer service is not deadline lateness.
The Stage 1 epoch callback precedes complete actor service and cannot silently own the Stage 2 summary boundary.
Actor_work_quantum remains legacy_current and non-forceable until cooperative checkpoints and exactly-once repost are separately designed and verified.
Buffer_copy_coalescing remains legacy_current and non-forceable until a distinct conservative implementation and exact terminal-release correlation are separately designed and verified.
Active_internal and production activation remain unauthorized.
alternatives_considered: Use existing aggregate metrics as the dataset contract. Rejected because they are not connection-attributable, versioned, or deterministically joinable.
Treat each dequeued event as one equal work unit. Rejected because packet, API, timer, effect, and follow-on costs differ materially.
Add a quantum while instrumenting the loop. Rejected because no exactly-once repost or reviewed preemption seam exists.
Insert the actor summary into the current Stage 1 epoch callback. Rejected because that callback occurs before complete actor service and would shift or truncate attribution.
risks: Observation overhead can perturb hot shard paths; disabled-path and later manual or nightly allocation checks remain required.
Partial per-connection coverage can be mistaken for complete wake membership; manifests must declare coverage.
A post-service fault can leave incomplete outcome information; bounded fault disposition remains explicit.
Primitive counts can be mistaken for a reviewed scalar quantum; UsefulWorkUnitsUndefined prevents that claim.
open_questions: Which post-service boundary will publish actor epoch summaries and join them to Stage 1 epochs without shifting attribution?
Which bounded shard-pressure snapshot can expose runnable connection count and oldest item age without a global lock?
